snippet.title: Michael Jackson - They Don't Care About Us (Completo) (Tradução/Legendado)
snippet.description:
﹏﹏✨﹏﹏﹏﹏✨﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏✨﹏﹏
Wikipedia: "They Don't Care About Us" é uma canção de protesto do Michael Jackson que foi lançada em 16 de junho de 1995 como o quarto single de trabalho do álbum HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I. A música foi uma das mais polêmicas de toda a carreira de Jackson. Acusado de fazer apologia ao antissemitismo pelos jornais, Michael alegou que não tinha a intenção de ferir ninguém e regravou a música, que é um hino contra as injustiças sociais. "They Don't Care About Us" é diferente de todo o estilo musical de Michael. A canção tem batidas de reggae e hip hop. Há ainda uma versão lançada no Brasil em parceria com o grupo baiano Olodum, que introduziu na canção elementos de samba-reggae.
Comercialmente, "They Don't Care About Us" tornou-se um sucesso entre os dez países europeus e número um na República Tcheca, Alemanha, Hungria e Itália. Nos EUA, a canção alcançou o número 30 na Billboard Hot 100.
"They Don't Care About Us" foi interpretada como parte de um medley com "Scream" e "In the Closet" durante a terceira e última série de concertos de Jackson, a HIStory World Tour,que durou de 1996 a 1997. A canção estava programada para ser apresentada na série de concertos de retorno de Jackson na O2 Arena, em Londres, de julho de 2009 a março de 2010, mas os shows foram cancelados devido à sua morte súbita em 25 de junho de 2009. "They Don't Care About Us" foi remixado com partes de canções como "Privacy" (do álbum Invincible) e "Tabloid Junkie" (do HIStory), e lançado no álbum Immortal, em novembro de 2011.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson na Favela Santa Marta?! A verdade que os guias escondem | PPTV
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson no coração de uma favela controlada por gangues? 😱
Parece inacreditável, mas foi exatamente isso que aconteceu.

Neste episódio especial, Pepe TV leva você até a favela Santa Marta, no Rio de Janeiro — um lugar onde, nos anos 90, até a polícia tinha medo de entrar. Foi aqui que Michael Jackson, ao lado do diretor Spike Lee, gravou cenas icônicas do clipe “They Don’t Care About Us”, mudando para sempre a história da música… e o destino da comunidade.

📍 Voltamos a 1996, quando Santa Marta era considerada uma das áreas mais perigosas do mundo, dominada por cartéis do tráfico. Para subir o morro, a equipe de Michael precisou negociar diretamente com líderes locais. O que parecia loucura se transformou em um marco de esperança.

🎶 Hoje, o local abriga a famosa “Laje do Michael Jackson”, com uma estátua de bronze do Rei do Pop e um enorme mosaico de Romero Britto. Turistas do mundo inteiro passam por ali — mas poucos conhecem toda a história por trás dessas escadas.

🇵🇱 Mas Pepe TV vai além.
Você sabia que existe um rastro polonês escondido nas favelas do Rio?

Há décadas, missionários poloneses (verbitas e palotinos) atuam silenciosamente em comunidades como Santa Marta, criando centros de apoio para crianças, educação básica e assistência médica. Um capítulo pouco conhecido da solidariedade internacional — e uma contribuição real da Polônia para a construção da paz social no Brasil.

💬 Esta não é apenas uma história sobre Michael Jackson.
É uma história sobre dignidade, empatia, cultura e transformação.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson w faweli Santa Marta. Szokująca prawda o Rio, gangach i… polskim śladzie | Pepe TV
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson w jednym z najniebezpieczniejszych miejsc Brazylii? Tak! Cofamy się do roku 1996, kiedy Król Popu wybrał favelę Santa Marta w Rio de Janeiro na plan swojego manifestu „They Don’t Care About Us”. To tutaj, w miejscu kontrolowanym niegdyś przez kartele narkotykowe, rozegrały się sceny, które odmieniły historię muzyki i losy tysięcy mieszkańców.

W materiale Pepe TV pokazujemy kulisy tej wizyty, negocjacje z lokalnymi bossami, rolę reżysera Spike’a Lee oraz to, jak obecność Michaela Jacksona dała Santa Marta „drugie życie” – czyniąc ją symbolem nadziei i pierwszą „spacyfikowaną” favelą.

Ale to nie wszystko. Szukamy głębiej i odkrywamy polski ślad w Rio de Janeiro, o którym nie mówią światowe przewodniki. Polscy misjonarze – werbiści i pallotyni – od lat działają w brazylijskich fawelach, tworząc świetlice dla dzieci i punkty pomocy medycznej. To cicha, ale realna pomoc płynąca z Polski w najtrudniejszych latach dziewięćdziesiątych.

Zobaczycie Laje do Michael Jackson, brązowy pomnik artysty, mozaikę Romero Britto i usłyszycie historie mieszkańców, którzy – podobnie jak Selarón ze swoimi schodami – rzeźbili własną godność, wykorzystując legendę Króla Popu jako tarczę przed zapomnieniem.

📍 Pepe TV zabiera Was tam, gdzie turyści boją się wejść sami.
🎥 Bez filtrów. Z polską perspektywą.

👉 Subskrybujcie, zostawcie łapkę w górę i udostępnijcie materiał, aby świat poznał polski ślad w Rio.

snippet.description:

Copied from Wikipedia:
"They Don't Care About Us" is a song written, produced and performed by American singer Michael Jackson, released on April 23, 1996, as the fourth single from his ninth album, HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I (1995). It is a protest song and remains one of the most controversial pieces Jackson ever composed. In the United States, media scrutiny surrounding allegations of antisemitic lyrics were the catalyst for Jackson issuing multiple clarifications, an apology, defense from director Spike Lee and re-releasing an edited version of the song. Jackson countered allegations of antisemitism, arguing that reviews had misinterpreted the context of the song, either unintentionally or deliberately.

"They Don't Care About Us" was accompanied by two music videos directed by Lee. The first was shot in two locations in Brazil: in Pelourinho, the historic city center of Salvador; and in Santa Marta, a favela of Rio de Janeiro.[6][7] State authorities tried to ban production over fears the video would damage their image, the area and prospects of Rio de Janeiro staging the 2004 Olympics. Still, the residents of the area were happy to see Jackson, hoping their problems would be made visible to a wider audience.[7] The second video was shot in a prison and contained video footage of multiple references to human rights abuses.

Commercially, "They Don't Care About Us" became a top ten hit in European countries and number one in the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary and Italy. In the US, the song peaked at number 30 on the Billboard Hot 100. The music video premiere was viewed by over 200 million people worldwide, making it one of the most viewed music videos. [8]

"They Don't Care About Us" was performed as part of a medley with "Scream" and "In the Closet" during Jackson's third and final concert series, the HIStory World Tour, which ran from 1996 to 1997. The song was set to be performed on Jackson's This Is It comeback concert series at The O2 Arena in London from July 2009 to March 2010, but the shows were cancelled due to his sudden death in June 2009. In 2011, the Immortal album included a remixed version of "They Don't Care About Us" which features elements of the songs "Privacy" (from Invincible) and "Tabloid Junkie" (from HIStory).

The song gained renewed attention and relevance due to its use during Black Lives Matter protests in 2014 and 2015, and again in 2020 with Spike Lee's "Director's Cut" of the music videos being combined, along with new footage of attacks against protestors.[9][10]

Music and composition:
The song begins with a group of children singing the chorus, "All I wanna say is that they don't really care about us". In between the chorus lines, one child chants, "Don't worry what people say, we know the truth", after which another child says, "Enough is enough of this garbage!"[11][12][13] It is played in the key of D minor and the track's time signature is common time.[14] The song, which is cited as being a pop song, has a moderately slow tempo of 90 beats per minute. Instruments used include synthesizers, percussion with Olodum and guitar.[14]

Critical reception:
Larry Flick from Billboard noted that the song's much-documented offending words were obscured by sound effects. He wrote, "With or without those words, this song comes across as less an intended indictment of the world's oppressive forces and more as lightly shrouded ramblings of personal paranoia. There is nothing wrong with an artist pouring personal experience into a song, of course, but the range of emotion displayed in Jackson's snarling vocal would be far more affecting within a more direct lyrical context."[15] A reviewer from Music Week rated "They Don't Care About Us" four out of five, adding, "With echoes of Bad, Jackson's next single from HIStory sees him in tougher mode, with some real raucous guitar backing his soaring vocals."[16] The magazine's Alan Jones described it as "a slim, sylph-like tirade, economical and angry." He concluded, "The quality of the song is there however, and Jacko's on a roll. Number one?"[17] Jim Farber of New York Daily News said that Jackson "snarled" while singing, that the song "clicked" and has an "original clattering rhythm".[18]

snippet.title: Michael Jackson's Iconic Filming Locations in Brazil- See Where All The Magic Happened!
snippet.description:
This is a video of my real-life experience traveling to both Rio de Janeiro and Salvador, Brazil to the  location Michael Jackson used to create his amazing music video "They Don't Care About Us". I visited both the favela Santa Marta in Rio where he filmed the first part of the video. 
Secondly, I flew to Salvador Bahia where he collaborated with the Brazilian group Olodum for tehe second part of the video. In Salvador, I entered the building Michael used to film his balcony scene and the courtyard of Pelourinho Square, Bahia.
 It was an unforgettable  experience and I am forever grateful for the opportunity I had to visit both locations. 

Twenty-five years ago, Michael Jackson and Olodum, the iconic Afro-Brazilian musical band, teamed up to film the music video for ‘They don’t care about us.’ Spike Lee was hired to make the short film for the song.

The film was shot in Salvador, Brazil on Feb.9. This date is known as the day when Michael Jackson took over Salvador, because the whole city literally stopped to see the King of Pop performing in the streets of the historic Pelourinho— a neighborhood that is located in the center area of Salvador. 

As Spike Lee explained during a presentation at TedX Brooklyn in 2013, Michael wanted him to make a “short film, not a music video” for a song from the upcoming album ‘HIStory.’

After the two agreed on the song, they traveled to Brazil, where Lee recommended using the Olodum drum team as part of the film production— the same musicians Paul Simon employed for his chart-topping album, ‘Rhythm of the Saints.’ The song goes as follow:

All I want to say is that they don't really care about us
Don't worry what people say, we know the truth

snippet.title: MASSIVE Michael Jackson Statues Around the World (You Can Visit These)
snippet.description:
🗽 There are giant Michael Jackson statues scattered across the planet right now — and you can actually visit most of them. We're talking 32-foot tall fiberglass titans, life-size bronze tributes, copper sculptures inside Buddhist temples, and one statue that famously floated down the River Thames in 1995 to promote an album.
In this video, we walk through every major Michael Jackson statue still standing around the world — where to find them, who built them, and the wild stories behind each one:
▪️ The 1995 HIStory Statues — Up to 10 giant fiberglass statues, each 32 feet tall and weighing 4,625 pounds, created by sculptor Derek Howarth and commissioned through artist Stephen Pyle. Debuted on the River Thames on June 15, 1995.
▪️ Magicland Theme Park, Rome — One of the original HIStory statues, fully restored in 2019 with fresh paint and new sunglasses.
▪️ Santarama Miniland, Johannesburg — Personally donated by Michael to the South African National Tuberculosis Association after the 1997 HIStory Tour.
▪️ Guangzhou Sculpture Park, China — A bronze funded entirely by Chinese fans who raised 158,000 yuan ($23,000), sculpted by Lu Zhenkang and unveiled January 1, 2011.
▪️ Shan Yuan Temple, Hong Kong — A copper Smooth Criminal statue commissioned by pop singer Alex To and installed inside an actual Buddhist temple on October 7, 2009.
▪️ Santa Marta Favela, Rio de Janeiro — A bronze standing on the exact concrete slab where Michael danced during the "They Don't Care About Us" video, next to a mosaic by artist Romero Britto.
▪️ Hard Rock Hotel, Penang, Malaysia — Michael depicted seated in a pose inspired by the Abraham Lincoln Memorial.
▪️ Mistelbach an der Zaya, Austria — A Smooth Criminal statue by sculptor Daniel Kartakova, funded entirely by Austrian MJ fans.
▪️ Mandalay Bay, Las Vegas — A HIStory statue displayed alongside the Michael Jackson ONE Cirque du Soleil show.
▪️ Center for Great Apes, Florida — A life-size bronze of Bubbles the chimpanzee holding a paintbrush, unveiled on April 12, 2025 — officially declared "Bubbles Day" by Wauchula's mayor.
We also cover the controversial Fulham FC statue (now in storage in Manchester), the cult-favorite McDonald's HIStory statue in Best, Netherlands (removed in 2019), and the three dedicated Michael Jackson forests in England and Turkey.
Michael's monuments span more than a dozen countries across five continents. The Brazilian statue stands on the concrete he danced on. The Hong Kong statue stands inside the temple of a friend he met in 1987. The Florida bronze stands where his beloved chimpanzee still lives today.
Whatever your opinion of the man, the geography of his monuments is undeniable. The statues are still there. People are still visiting. Fans are still leaving flowers.

Copied from Wikipedia:
"They Don't Care About Us" is a song written, produced and performed by American singer Michael Jackson, released on April 23, 1996, as the fourth single from his ninth album, HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I (1995). It is a protest song and remains one of the most controversial pieces Jackson ever composed. In the United States, media scrutiny surrounding allegations of antisemitic lyrics were the catalyst for Jackson issuing multiple clarifications, an apology, defense from director Spike Lee and re-releasing an edited version of the song. Jackson countered allegations of antisemitism, arguing that reviews had misinterpreted the context of the song, either unintentionally or deliberately.

"They Don't Care About Us" was accompanied by two music videos directed by Lee. The first was shot in two locations in Brazil: in Pelourinho, the historic city center of Salvador; and in Santa Marta, a favela of Rio de Janeiro.[6][7] State authorities tried to ban production over fears the video would damage their image, the area and prospects of Rio de Janeiro staging the 2004 Olympics. Still, the residents of the area were happy to see Jackson, hoping their problems would be made visible to a wider audience.[7] The second video was shot in a prison and contained video footage of multiple references to human rights abuses.

Commercially, "They Don't Care About Us" became a top ten hit in European countries and number one in the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary and Italy. In the US, the song peaked at number 30 on the Billboard Hot 100. The music video premiere was viewed by over 200 million people worldwide, making it one of the most viewed music videos. [8]

"They Don't Care About Us" was performed as part of a medley with "Scream" and "In the Closet" during Jackson's third and final concert series, the HIStory World Tour, which ran from 1996 to 1997. The song was set to be performed on Jackson's This Is It comeback concert series at The O2 Arena in London from July 2009 to March 2010, but the shows were cancelled due to his sudden death in June 2009. In 2011, the Immortal album included a remixed version of "They Don't Care About Us" which features elements of the songs "Privacy" (from Invincible) and "Tabloid Junkie" (from HIStory).

The song gained renewed attention and relevance due to its use during Black Lives Matter protests in 2014 and 2015, and again in 2020 with Spike Lee's "Director's Cut" of the music videos being combined, along with new footage of attacks against protestors.[9][10]

Music and composition:
The song begins with a group of children singing the chorus, "All I wanna say is that they don't really care about us". In between the chorus lines, one child chants, "Don't worry what people say, we know the truth", after which another child says, "Enough is enough of this garbage!"[11][12][13] It is played in the key of D minor and the track's time signature is common time.[14] The song, which is cited as being a pop song, has a moderately slow tempo of 90 beats per minute. Instruments used include synthesizers, percussion with Olodum and guitar.[14]

Critical reception:
Larry Flick from Billboard noted that the song's much-documented offending words were obscured by sound effects. He wrote, "With or without those words, this song comes across as less an intended indictment of the world's oppressive forces and more as lightly shrouded ramblings of personal paranoia. There is nothing wrong with an artist pouring personal experience into a song, of course, but the range of emotion displayed in Jackson's snarling vocal would be far more affecting within a more direct lyrical context."[15] A reviewer from Music Week rated "They Don't Care About Us" four out of five, adding, "With echoes of Bad, Jackson's next single from HIStory sees him in tougher mode, with some real raucous guitar backing his soaring vocals."[16] The magazine's Alan Jones described it as "a slim, sylph-like tirade, economical and angry." He concluded, "The quality of the song is there however, and Jacko's on a roll. Number one?"[17] Jim Farber of New York Daily News said that Jackson "snarled" while singing, that the song "clicked" and has an "original clattering rhythm".[18]

"They Don't Care About Us" is a song by the American singer Michael Jackson, released on April 8, 1996, in the UK, and April 23 in the US. It was the fourth single from Jackson's ninth album, HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I (1995).

The initial release contained ethnic slurs, triggering accusations of antisemitism. Jackson issued an apology, saying the lyrics had been intended to draw attention to social injustice, and altered future copies.

Two music videos were directed by Spike Lee. The first was shot in Pelourinho, the historic city center of Salvador, and in Santa Marta, a favela of Rio de Janeiro. State authorities tried to ban production over fears the video would damage their image, the area and prospects of Rio de Janeiro staging the 2004 Olympics. Still, the residents of the area were happy to see Jackson, hoping their problems would be made visible to a wider audience. The second video was shot in a prison and contains footage of human rights abuses.

"They Don't Care About Us" became a top-10 hit in European countries and number one in the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, and Italy. In the US, it reached number 30 on the Billboard Hot 100. The music video premiere was viewed by over 200 million people worldwide, making it one of the most viewed music videos.

Jackson performed "They Don't Care About Us" as part of a medley with "Scream" and "In the Closet" during his third and final concert series, the HIStory World Tour, which ran from 1996 to 1997. The song was set to be performed on Jackson's This Is It comeback concert series July 2009 to March 2010, but the shows were cancelled due to his death in June 2009. In 2011, the Immortal album included a remixed version of "They Don't Care About Us", with elements of the songs "Privacy" (from Invincible) and "Tabloid Junkie" (from HIStory).

The song gained renewed attention due to its use during Black Lives Matter protests in 2014 and 2015, and again in 2020 with Spike Lee's "Director's Cut" of the music videos being combined, along with new footage of attacks against protestors.

The music video was directed by Spike Lee. Asked why he chose Lee to direct the video, Jackson responded, "'They Don't Care About Us' has an edge, and Spike Lee had approached me. It's a public awareness song and that's what he is all about. It's a protest kind of song ... and I think he was perfect for it". Speaking to William E. Ketchum III of Stereogum in 2025, Lee recounted that Jackson had contacted him prior to the release of HIStory, and asked him to pick one song from the record to direct a music video for. Lee initially selected "Stranger in Moscow", but Jackson encouraged him to direct the video for "They Don't Care About Us" instead.

Jackson also collaborated with 200 members of the cultural group Olodum, who "swayed to the heavy beat of Salvador's 'samba-reggae' music". The media interest surrounding the music video exposed Olodum to 140 countries around the world, bringing them worldwide fame and increased credibility in Brazil. At the beginning of the video, a Brazilian woman says, "Michael, eles não ligam pra gente" (Portuguese for "Michael, they don't care about us"), recorded by Angélica Vieira, producer of Manhattan Connection.

peaking of the music video, in The New Brazilian Cinema, Lúcia Nagib observed:

When Michael Jackson decided to shoot his new music video in a favela of Rio de Janeiro ... he used the favela people as extras in a visual super-spectacle ... All the while there is a vaguely political appeal in there ... The interesting aspect of Michael Jackson's strategy is the efficiency with which it gives visibility to poverty and social problems in countries like Brazil without resorting to traditional political discourse. The problematic aspect is that it does not entail a real intervention in that poverty.
